root_cause.text: `security/integrity/ima/ima_fs.c:create_securityfs_measurement_lists()` unconditionally indexed `hash_algo_name[algo]` for each TPM bank, but unsupported TPM algorithms were stored as `HASH_ALGO__LAST`, causing an out-of-bounds read when creating IMA securityfs measurement files.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description says `ima_tpm_chip->allocated_banks[i].crypto_id is initialized to HASH_ALGO__LAST if the TPM algorithm is not supported` and reports a KASAN `global-out-of-bounds in create_securityfs_measurement_lists` on `hash_algo_name`; the patch fixes this by checking `if (algo == HASH_ALGO__LAST)` and using `"_tpm_alg_%x"` with `allocated_banks[i].alg_id` instead of indexing `hash_algo_name[algo]`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use TPM algorithm IDs in securityfs measurement filenames when no standard hash algorithm name is available.
intent_record.what: The code now conditionally changes the securityfs measurement file names when `algo == HASH_ALGO__LAST`. In that case, it formats the ASCII and binary runtime measurement filenames using `tpm_alg_%x` and `ima_tpm_chip->allocated_banks[i].alg_id` instead of using `hash_algo_name[algo]`. For all other algorithms, the original filename formatting is unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this allows measurement list files to be created with a TPM algorithm identifier when the algorithm does not map to a standard hash name, avoiding an invalid or unusable name lookup. This makes the exported securityfs entries distinguishable and usable for TPM bank algorithms that are represented by the sentinel `HASH_ALGO__LAST`.

grouping_result.intent: Use TPM algorithm IDs in securityfs measurement filenames when no standard hash algorithm name is available.

relevance_review.reason: The change addresses the same code path and behavior as the bug: generating IMA securityfs measurement filenames for TPM banks when a standard hash name is unavailable. This is directly related to handling unsupported TPM algorithms instead of blindly indexing the hash-algorithm name table, which caused the out-of-bounds read.

candidates.rationale: This statement directly formats the securityfs filename using a hash algorithm name, and in the vulnerable code it was paired with an unconditional index into hash_algo_name[algo]. If algo held HASH_ALGO__LAST for an unsupported TPM bank, this path could trigger the out-of-bounds read.

This is the exact out-of-bounds access described in the root cause: unsupported TPM algorithms were stored as HASH_ALGO__LAST, and indexing hash_algo_name[algo] without validation could read past the array bounds.
Like the ASCII case, this statement participates in constructing measurement filenames from hash_algo_name[algo] and is vulnerable for the same reason when unsupported TPM algorithms are present.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the exact out-of-bounds array index described in the root cause. When an unsupported TPM bank was represented as HASH_ALGO__LAST, indexing hash_algo_name[algo] could read past the end of the array while constructing IMA securityfs measurement filenames.

This statement is part of the vulnerable filename construction path that used hash_algo_name[algo] unconditionally. By itself it contributes to the unsafe use of the algorithm-derived name when unsupported TPM algorithms are present.

This statement is the analogous filename construction for the binary measurements file and participates in the same vulnerable path that formats filenames using hash_algo_name[algo] without validating the TPM algorithm value.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is not present here. The bug root cause was an unconditional out-of-bounds index into `hash_algo_name[algo]` when an unsupported TPM algorithm was stored as `HASH_ALGO__LAST`. In this version, `create_securityfs_measurement_lists()` only iterates over `i < securityfs_measurement_list_count`, where the count is derived from `NR_BANKS(ima_tpm_chip)` and may be incremented only to add a SHA1 legacy entry: `securityfs_measurement_list_count = NR_BANKS(ima_tpm_chip); if (ima_sha1_idx >= NR_BANKS(ima_tpm_chip)) securityfs_measurement_list_count++;`. The file creation loop uses `algo = ima_algo_array[i].algo;` and then `hash_algo_name[algo]`, but this commit is specifically adding the measurement-list infrastructure and does not show the old unsupported-algorithm path from the vulnerable code. The actual readout paths now also route through `lookup_template_data_hash_algo()` and default to `algo = HASH_ALGO_SHA1`, so the shown function body already contains the new handling and does not clearly exhibit the original vulnerable construct.
